text:
infra-bot: ALERT: eu-west1 GPU pool degraded — NIC flaps on node group gw-rt-3, ~60% capacity loss. Automated traffic steering to us-west1 triggered. Incident INC-2029-045 created.
sara: Confirmed steering started at 12:03 UTC. User-facing 502/504 errors from EU clients spiked at the same time. Some requests still hit eu-west1 according to ingress logs.
matt: Checked public resolvers (8.8.8.8 / 1.1.1.1) and a few ISP resolvers — many still returning the old A records for api.redwood.ai. Our authoritative TTL was 300s. Looks like resolver holdovers.
ashley: We can drop authoritative TTL to 30s immediately, but that only helps new lookups. Stuff already cached won't fall back. Also some resolvers clamp TTLs to higher minimums, so propagation may still be slow.
sara: What's the risk of adding a short-lived CNAME like api-redirect.redwood.ai -> us-west1-proxy.redwood.ai and then swapping clients? Might bypass cached A records if the client does a fresh lookup for the CNAME.
leo: CNAME trick can work for clients that re-resolve hostnames, but many SDKs reuse DNS results for socket lifetime. Another lever: update our edge LB to respond with HTTP 307/302 pointing to us-west1 endpoint for requests that still land on eu-west1, then short-circuit heavy GPU work there. That avoids a DNS round trip for those requests.
matt: Good point. But we saw a non-trivial fraction (~7%) of traffic still failing at TCP handshake stage because resolvers return unreachables. 302 won't help there.
ashley: Two parallel actions I propose: 1) lower TTL to 30 and push change (already queued), 2) run a targeted resolver cache priming job to force re-resolution from major public ISPs and known problematic resolver IPs. That should reduce the reservoir of stale answers faster.
sara: I'm running the TTL change now. Ops: please validate once it lands.
ops-bot: DNS change applied: api.redwood.ai TTL set from 300 -> 30 at 12:07:41 UTC. Change propagated to our authoritative nameservers.
leo: Priming script ready. We'll hit endpoints from vantage points that mimic Google Public DNS, Cloudflare, major EU ISP resolvers, and some mobile resolvers. Script:
```
for ip in 8.8.8.8 1.1.1.1 195.66.16.16 80.58.61.250; do
  dig @${ip} api.redwood.ai +short || true
  curl -sS --resolve "api.redwood.ai:443:$(dig +short @${ip} api.redwood.ai | tail -n1)" https://api.redwood.ai/health || true
done
```
leo: Running from 6 endpoints in parallel, will monitor TTLs returned and connection success.
matt: Meanwhile, we need capacity — us-west1 is seeing a 2.8x increase in GPU utilization. We have ephemeral burst quota in Dedicated pool we can pull from, but it costs ~2.4x on top of normal. If we don't spin they will hit queued states and latency SLOs will break.
ashley: I can trigger an ephemeral scale + pre-warm script for 12 NVIDIAs in us-west1 now. Estimated cost delta ~ $3.2k/hr but it keeps tail latency under SLA. Requesting approval to proceed.
sara: Approved — do it. Prioritize critical customer tokens list (docs/slo/critical_tokens) for immediate routing to pre-warmed instances.
ops-bot: Ephemeral pool scale request submitted: +12 gpus -> provisioning. ETA ~4m.
leo: Quick note on routing: I'll add an LB rule to prefer warm nodes for requests with header x-client-tier=critical so we don't mix cold starts. That reduces risk of QoS violations.
matt: Post-priming check: dig @195.66.16.16 @8.8.8.8 now return the us-west1 A set for most queries, connection success rate improving from 84% -> 97% in last 5m. Edge logs show decreasing 502 counts.
sara: Great. Follow-up items: - keep TTL 30 for 15m then bump back to 300 when stable - run a resolver coverage priming once per region in runbook - add an automated pre-failover step to lower TTL to 60 in the next RC of steward automation - document cost delta and tag invoice codes for ephemeral burst.
ashley: I'll capture the cost / commit ids and put a summary in the incident ticket. Also adding a post-incident action: we should pre-provision a small warm pool in secondary regions for critical customers to avoid full-blow bursts.
leo: Also file a small ops automation to probe a matrix of public resolvers weekly and record TTL clamp behavior per ISP — saves guesswork next time.
matt: Closing loop: us-west1 provision completed at 12:13 UTC, cache priming shows >99% resolution to us-west1 across our probe set. Marking the immediate outage mitigated.
infra-bot: INCIDENT UPDATE: INC-2029-045 mitigated — eu-west1 degraded but traffic successfully steered. Postmortem assigned to @ashley.
sara: Thanks team. We'll keep monitoring for 2 hours and then release a short status note to customers about temporary failover and cost impact.
ops-bot: Note: saved run commands and dig outputs to /incidents/INC-2029-045/artifacts/dns-priming.log
matt: Adding final ask: let's include a TTL-playbook snippet in runbooks/incidents/dns-failover.md so runbook ops are prescriptive next time (exact commands, revert steps, and cost estimates).
ashley: Will draft the runbook PR after the postmortem.
ops-bot: Thread closed for updates; monitoring channel will remain open for 2h.
